program.title: Work and its sign
program.learning_goal: Decide whether a force adds energy, removes energy, or does no work.

core1a.title: A guide: the moving crate
core1a.authored_question: A 10 N friction force acts left while a crate slides 3 m right. What work does friction do?
walkthrough_steps: Choose the motion direction: 3 m right.
Choose the force direction: 10 N left.
Calculate W = 10 × 3 × cos 180° = −30 J.
Interpret the sign: friction removes mechanical energy from the moving crate.
core1a.conditions: Constant 10 N force, straight 3 m displacement, and no change of force direction within this step.

core1b.title: Your turn: two journeys
core1b.authored_question: A robot travels 4 m to the right while a 6 N braking force acts left. It then travels 2 m to the left while a 4 N resistive force acts right. What is the combined work done by these two resistive forces?
core1b.change_of_conditions: Two sequential displacement directions; requires tracking the sign twice rather than copying one-step friction arithmetic.

program.scope_note: For change of kinetic energy per distance, the relevant force is net tangential force; source Q7 wording remains unqualified.

program.title: Momentum and kinetic energy
program.learning_goal: Explain why equal momentum does not imply equal kinetic energy.

core1a.title: A guide: a toy trolley’s energy
core1a.authored_question: A 2 kg toy trolley has momentum 6 kg·m/s. How much kinetic energy does it have?
walkthrough_steps: Find the speed v=p/m=6/2=3 m/s.
Find kinetic energy K=½mv²=½×2×3²=9 J.
Check using K=p²/(2m)=36/4=9 J.
Compare the same 2 kg trolley at momentum magnitudes 0, 2, 6 and 10 kg·m/s: kinetic energies 0, 1, 9 and 25 J; a curved, not linear, K-versus-p relationship.
core1a.conditions: Classical, nonrelativistic momentum; the stated momentum and mass are measured in one inertial frame.

core1b.title: Your turn: two mystery toy carts
core1b.authored_question: A class measures two toy carts. Cart A has mass 2 kg and momentum magnitude 4 kg·m/s. Cart B has mass 4 kg and momentum magnitude 8 kg·m/s. Which cart has more kinetic energy, and by how much?
core1b.change_of_conditions: Unlike the guide's single trolley or fixed-mass table, both momentum and mass change. The learner must select K=p²/(2m) for each and compare resulting values, rather than apply one fixed-variable rule.

program.scope_note: Q2, Q4 and Q8 theme grouping, learner-facing candidate only; guided same-mass pattern table, same-energy and same-momentum boundaries; no QRT classification assigned.

program.title: Energy and where motion is possible
program.learning_goal: Find accessible regions, identify energy barriers and distinguish K = 0 from impossible motion.

core1a.title: A guide: a cart climbing a hill
core1a.authored_question: A 1 kg cart has total mechanical energy 50 J on a smooth track. At a point 3 m above the reference level, find its kinetic energy and speed (g = 10 m/s²).
walkthrough_steps: Calculate U = 1 × 10 × 3 = 30 J.
Find K = E − U = 50 − 30 = 20 J.
Use K = ½mv², giving v = √40 ≈ 6.32 m/s.
At a turning point K can be zero; negative K is physically impossible.
core1a.conditions: Smooth track, negligible dissipative forces, fixed gravitational reference, constant g and a particle moving along the connected track.

core1b.title: Your turn: can the cart cross?
core1b.authored_question: A 1 kg cart starts in a left valley at height 1 m. Its total mechanical energy is 50 J. The track rises to a 6 m high ridge, then falls to a right valley at 3 m. Take g = 10 m/s². No motor or friction acts. Can the cart reach the right valley from the left?
core1b.change_of_conditions: An energy barrier blocks access to an otherwise allowed destination; this is a path-reasoning transfer, not another endpoint-speed calculation.

program.title: Potential energy and force direction
program.source_gate_note: Source wording omits the minus sign
program.learning_goal: Read the slope of a potential-energy curve to infer the direction of conservative force.

core1a.title: A guide: a sloping potential
core1a.authored_question: A particle has U(x) = 12 J − (3 N)x. What is the constant conservative force along x?
walkthrough_steps: Differentiate U(x) = 12 − 3x, so dU/dx = −3 N.
Apply the negative gradient: Fₓ = −(−3 N) = +3 N.
The force points toward increasing x, where potential energy decreases.
Specify the interval where this potential law is differentiable.
core1a.conditions: One-dimensional conservative force, differentiable potential over the interval, consistent coordinates and units.

core1b.title: Your turn: an unfamiliar graph
core1b.authored_question: A piecewise-linear potential has U = 2 J at x = 0 m, U = 10 J at x = 2 m, then U = 4 J at x = 4 m. Which statement about the conservative force is correct between these points?
core1b.change_of_conditions: Interpret two different piecewise-linear slopes on their open intervals instead of differentiating one algebraic expression. The challenge does not directly test the undefined force at the sharp corner; that issue belongs to its worked check.

program.title: Explosions and energy transfer
program.source_gate_note: Initial motion not specified in source
program.learning_goal: Distinguish momentum conservation from kinetic-energy conservation during an internal release.

core1a.title: A guide: two carts pushed apart
core1a.authored_question: Two linked carts, masses 1 kg and 3 kg, start at rest on a frictionless track. A spring pushes the 1 kg cart to the right at 3 m/s. Find the 3 kg cart's velocity.
walkthrough_steps: Initial total momentum: 0 kg·m/s.
Final balance: (1 kg)(+3 m/s) + (3 kg)v = 0.
Solve v = −1 m/s, so the heavier cart moves left.
Final total kinetic energy is 4.5 + 1.5 = 6 J, supplied by the spring.
core1a.conditions: System initially at rest, negligible external horizontal impulse, spring energy released, nonrelativistic motion.

core1b.title: Your turn: the parent cart was moving
core1b.authored_question: A 2 kg cart is initially moving right at 4 m/s. It splits into a 0.5 kg part moving right at 10 m/s and a 1.5 kg part. External horizontal impulse is negligible. What is the heavier part's velocity, and how much does total kinetic energy change?
core1b.change_of_conditions: The parent initially moves; the two fragments can both move right in the laboratory frame, unlike the rest-start guide.
